sub_criteria.name: extraction accuracy
sub_criteria.text: Measures LLM claim-extraction accuracy from full papers or abstracts against expert/human annotation, ideally broken down by paper section, claim type, or model.

sub_criteria.name: evidence-link errors
sub_criteria.text: Characterizes how claim-to-evidence links (passage, table, or citation) fail: fabricated support, wrong-direction reads of contradicting evidence, or over-generalisation past the paper's conditions.

sub_criteria.name: benchmark construction
sub_criteria.text: Describes how a claim-evidence or citation-grounding benchmark (e.g. SciFact, CiteME, or similar) was built, and what its reported numbers can or cannot legitimately support.

sub_criteria.name: abstention and calibration
sub_criteria.text: Tests whether abstention or calibrated uncertainty improves the trustworthiness of extracted claims, and reports the coverage cost of doing so.

sub_criteria.name: cross-model or cross-domain generalisation
sub_criteria.text: Reports whether extraction or grounding results replicate across different models, domains, or paper types, or whether they are inflated by benchmark artifacts.

items.abstract_600: Technology scouting and competitive intelligence increasingly rely on rapid access to scientific and technical evidence. Large language models (LLMs) are reshaping question answering by enabling users to express exploratory and evolving information needs in natural language. However, their usefulness is limited by hallucinations, weak calibration, poor abstention when evidence is missing, and the cost of keeping knowledge up to date. items.title: CTIFoundry: An Agent-Native Corpus Scaffold for Cyber Threat Intelligence
items.abstract_600: Cyber threat intelligence (CTI) is increasingly consumed not by human analysts but by LLM agents that compose multi-step investigations at query time. The harness side of this shift has matured rapidly (planning loops, tool protocols, context management), but the corpus side has not: threat reports and vulnerability databases are still packaged for retrieval-augmented generation, as opaque chunks behind an embedding index. items.title: GraphCheck: Breaking Long-Term Text Barriers with Extracted Knowledge Graph-Powered Fact-Checking
items.abstract_600: Large language models (LLMs) are widely used, but they often generate subtle factual errors, especially in long-form text. These errors are fatal in some specialized domains such as medicine. Existing fact-checking with grounding documents methods face two main challenges: (1) they struggle to understand complex multihop relations in long documents, often overlooking subtle factual errors; (2) most specialized methods rely on pairwise comparisons, requiring multiple model calls, leading to high resource and computational costs. items.title: Impact of extraction techniques on phytochemical composition and bioactivity of natural product mixtures
items.abstract_600: Extraction methods critically influence the phytochemical profile and bioactivity of natural product mixtures, affecting their efficacy as therapeutic agents. This review assesses the impact of various extraction techniques-such as solvent-based extraction, ultrasound-assisted extraction, and enzymatic extraction-on the composition of bioactive compounds in plant extracts. items.abstract_600: BACKGROUND: Large language models (LLMs) have gained prominence since the release of ChatGPT in late 2022. items.abstract_600: Biomedical fact-checking systems must do more than predict whether a claim is supported, contradicted, or unaddressed: they should also produce evidence that is faithful, complete, and useful for verification. items.abstract_600: LLMs have demonstrated impressive proficiency in generating coherent and high-quality text, making them valuable across a range of text-generation tasks. items.abstract_600: Rust is a modern systems programming language whose ownership-based type system statically guarantees memory safety, making it particularly well-suited to the domain of safety-critical systems. In recent years, a wellspring of automated deductive verification tools have emerged for establishing functional correctness of Rust code. items.abstract_600: The profusion of knowledge encoded in large language models (LLMs) and their ability to apply this knowledge zero-shot in a range of settings makes them promising candidates for use in decision-making. However, they are currently limited by their inability to provide outputs which can be faithfully explained and effectively contested to correct mistakes. items.abstract_600: Evidence synthesis is crucial for turning primary research into reliable knowledge for science, medicine, education, and policy. items.abstract_600: Accurate interpretation of genomic variants is critical for precision oncology but remains slow and dependent on specialized expertise. items.abstract_600: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed in scientific research, where reliability is critical and the underlying knowledge is densely interconnected.
